gaps.hint: negative adjective needed (-ish): not appropriate for an adult
gaps.explanation: 'Childish' is negative (silly, immature); 'childlike' is positive (innocent). The embarrassment shows the negative sense.

gaps.sentence: The prison was ___ , with three men in cells meant for one (CROWDED).
gaps.hint: too full — more people than the space allows (over-)
gaps.explanation: Three men in one cell means too crowded: overcrowded (over- + crowded). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: She ___ admitted that she had made a mistake (HONEST).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ly forms adverbs: honestly modifies the verb 'admitted'.

gaps.sentence: She gave a very ___ account of the incident that had everyone laughing (HUMOUR).
gaps.explanation: Everyone laughed, so the adjective is humorous (-ous). 'Humourless' means serious and would contradict the laughter.

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: The instructions were unclear, so I had to ___ them completely (WRITE).
gaps.hint: write again — unclear the first time (re-); base verb needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix re- means again: rewrite. A base verb is needed after 'had to'.

gaps.sentence: The mixture will ___ as it cools (SOLID).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: solidify means to become solid. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: The company is a major ___ (EMPLOY) in the region.
gaps.hint: the company gives jobs — it is the one who employs
gaps.explanation: An employer gives work; an employee receives it. The sentence is about the company.
